meaning.en: To lend support to an event or a friend by showing up and filling the room.
meaning.zh: 到场助阵，替人撑起场面。

examples.zh: 他开新店，朋友们都来撑场子。
examples.en: When he opened the new shop, friends all came to show support.

examples.zh: 今晚的演出你一定要来给我撑撑场子。
examples.en: You must come tonight and back me up at the show.

usage.en: Friendly. Compare 撑场面, which is about making things look impressive; 砸场子 is the opposite.
usage.zh: 带善意；与侧重排场的“撑场面”不同，反义“砸场子”。

meaning.en: To do something one is ashamed of in one's heart.

examples.zh: 人不能做亏心事，否则夜里睡不着。
examples.en: One mustn't do shameful things, or one can't sleep at night.

examples.zh: 他做了亏心事，一见警察就心慌。
examples.en: He did something shameful and panics at the sight of police.

usage.en: Often paired with 不怕鬼敲门: 白天不做亏心事，半夜不怕鬼敲门.
usage.zh: 常见搭配“不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门”。

meaning.en: To act only for show, without real effort or sincerity.
meaning.zh: 只做表面功夫给人看，并不真心实意。

examples.zh: 他们检查只是做样子，根本没认真。
examples.en: Their inspection was just for show; they weren't serious.

examples.zh: 你别光做样子，要动真格的。
examples.en: Don't just go through the motions; do it for real.

usage.en: Mildly critical; often 只是/不过是做样子.
usage.zh: 略带批评，常说“只是做样子”。

meaning.en: To say or do something auspicious to attract good luck.
meaning.zh: 说吉利话或做吉利事，求个好兆头。

examples.zh: 春节大家都去庙会讨彩头。
examples.en: At Spring Festival everyone goes to the temple fair to seek good luck.

examples.zh: 他买了个吉利号码，就是想讨个彩头。
examples.en: He bought a lucky number just to get a good omen.

usage.en: Also 讨口彩 (say lucky words). 彩头 = prize or good omen, from gambling and festivities.
usage.zh: 也说“讨口彩”。“彩头”指奖品或吉兆。

meaning.en: To secretly harm someone, especially a friend who trusted you.
meaning.zh: 暗地里伤害别人，尤指信任自己的人。

examples.zh: 他表面上是朋友，背后捅刀子。
examples.en: He's a friend on the surface but stabs you in the back.

examples.zh: 我最恨在背后捅刀子的人。
examples.en: I hate people who stab you in the back most.

usage.en: Shortened to 捅刀子, which can also mean to attack openly with cutting words.
usage.zh: 可简说“捅刀子”，也可指用话刺伤人。

meaning.en: To give a formal warning that further misconduct will be punished.
meaning.zh: 正式警告，再犯将受处罚。

examples.zh: 监管部门对这家公司亮出了黄牌。
examples.en: The regulator showed the company a yellow card.

examples.zh: 老师给迟到的学生亮黄牌。
examples.en: The teacher gave the late students a yellow card.

usage.en: From football. Next stage: 亮红牌. Usually 亮出黄牌 / 给……亮黄牌.
usage.zh: 来自足球，更严重为“亮红牌”。

meaning.en: A person who thinks in one narrow way and will not adapt.
meaning.zh: 认死理、不知变通的人或性格。

examples.zh: 他是个一根筋，劝不动。
examples.en: He has a one-track mind and can't be persuaded.

examples.zh: 做事别一根筋，要学会变通。
examples.en: Don't be single-minded; learn to be flexible.

usage.en: Casual, can be a mild tease. The image is of having only one nerve to think with.

meaning.en: The leading position in an organisation or field.
meaning.zh: 首领或在某领域居首位的地位。

examples.zh: 他坐上了公司第一把交椅。
examples.en: He took the top chair in the company.

examples.zh: 这位教练稳坐球队第一把交椅。
examples.en: The coach firmly holds the top post at the club.

usage.en: From the folding chairs of bandit chiefs and officials in vernacular fiction; often 坐第一把交椅.
usage.zh: 源于白话小说中头领所坐的交椅，常说“坐第一把交椅”。

meaning.en: To look at someone or something with prejudice.

examples.zh: 别戴有色眼镜看外地人。
examples.en: Don't look at outsiders with prejudice.

examples.zh: 他戴着有色眼镜，怎么看别人都不顺眼。
examples.en: With his tinted glasses on, he finds fault in everyone.

usage.en: Usually 戴着有色眼镜看…. Colour tints how everything looks.

meaning.en: To enjoy the fruits of others' labour without doing the work.

examples.zh: 我们辛苦干活，却让他来摘桃子。
examples.en: We work hard, then he comes to pick the peaches.

examples.zh: 不要总想着摘桃子，先做出贡献。
examples.en: Don't always wait to pick peaches; contribute first.

usage.en: Complaint, often 来摘桃子 or 坐享其成. Reference to peaches being picked by whoever comes last.
usage.zh: 多带不满，常说“来摘桃子”。

natural: find something to use against someone

meaning.en: To find a weakness or fault in someone to use against them.
meaning.zh: 抓住别人的错处作为要挟或攻击的依据。

examples.zh: 他们想抓你的把柄，做事要小心。
examples.en: They want something on you, so be careful.

examples.zh: 别让人抓住把柄。
examples.en: Don't let anyone get hold of something on you.

usage.en: Often 被人抓住把柄 or 抓……的把柄. 把柄 = handle, something to grab on to.

meaning.en: To come and disrupt someone's event, or damage their business.
meaning.zh: 故意去捣乱，破坏别人的场合或生意。

examples.zh: 有人来酒吧砸场子，被保安赶了出去。
examples.en: Someone came to wreck the bar and was thrown out by security.

examples.zh: 别来砸场子，今天是大喜的日子。
examples.en: Don't come to disrupt things; today is a happy occasion.

usage.en: Origin: street performers and martial-arts halls whose place got trashed. Opposite of 撑场子.
usage.zh: 源于江湖卖艺、武馆被人上门闹事。反义“撑场子”。

meaning.en: To damage a reputation built up over time.

examples.zh: 这样粗制滥造，会砸了咱们的招牌。
examples.en: Such shoddy work will ruin our reputation.

examples.zh: 一次食物中毒就砸了老店的招牌。
examples.en: One food-poisoning case smashed the old shop's good name.

usage.en: Usually 砸了……的招牌. 招牌 = shop signboard, reputation.

meaning.en: To get rid of troublesome people or problems that hold things up.

examples.zh: 村里的拆迁工作要先拔钉子。
examples.en: In the village's demolition, the 'nails' have to be removed first.

examples.zh: 这些年他一直在拔钉子，清理历史遗留问题。
examples.en: Over the years he has pulled out nails, clearing leftover problems.

usage.en: The 钉子 are the holdouts, 钉子户 (nail households); common in news about demolition.
usage.zh: “钉子”指拒不配合的人，常见于拆迁新闻。

meaning.en: To bully the weak and avoid the strong.

examples.zh: 他专捏软柿子，不敢惹强的。
examples.en: He only picks on the weak and dares not offend the strong.

examples.zh: 你想捏软柿子，也得看看我是谁。
examples.en: If you want to squeeze a soft target, check who I am first.

usage.en: Often 当软柿子捏. Persimmons: ripe ones squash easily.

meaning.en: To talk or argue at length, often with little result.
meaning.zh: 说个没完或反复劝说，却没有实效。

equivalents: talk till one is blue in the face

examples.zh: 我磨了半天嘴皮子，他还是不答应。
examples.en: I talked myself hoarse and he still wouldn't agree.

examples.zh: 别光磨嘴皮子，动手做吧。
examples.en: Stop talking and get on with it.

usage.en: Casual. Sometimes neutral for a patient talker; mostly dismissive.

natural: take a mile when given an inch

meaning.en: To become more demanding and rude whenever treated with leniency.

equivalents: give them an inch and they take a mile

examples.zh: 你对他好点，他就蹬鼻子上脸。
examples.en: Be a bit kind to him and he gets cheeky.

examples.zh: 别蹬鼻子上脸，我的耐心有限。
examples.en: Don't push your luck; my patience has limits.

usage.en: Often 别蹬鼻子上脸 as a warning; also 得寸进尺 as a literary parallel.
usage.zh: 常用作警告“别蹬鼻子上脸”。

meaning.en: To say harsh or threatening words, usually while leaving angrily.

examples.zh: 他气呼呼地撂下狠话就走了。
examples.en: He angrily dropped a threat and left.

examples.zh: 别动不动就撂狠话，大家好好谈。
examples.en: Stop throwing threats around; let's talk properly.

usage.en: Usually 撂下狠话 or 撂了句狠话. 撂 = drop or leave behind.
